SURFACE CONCEPT SEED (key: oracle-key-4; mode: experience; source: local; catalog: phoenix-2026-01; approved pool: d79644e7d5df; 24/24 catalog-curated; rerun with --scope surface --mode experience --from oracle-key-4 --reroll 1 --candidate-count 7 to reproduce this roll against this catalog revision)
RE-ROLL ROUND 1: every candidate presented in earlier rounds, grounded
  and challenger alike, is eliminated and may not return reworded. Derive
  genuinely new grounded candidates from unexplored angles before judging
  these fresh challengers.
DEALT INDICES: 7, 3, 6 (index 7 leads)
  After ordering the task's grounded structural candidates by resonance,
  deal candidates 7, 3, 6 of your own grounded list to the
  table; index 7 leads, and the deal never points at a challenger.
  The deal is the roll, not a suggestion: the dice decide which structures
  reach the user, so the ranking rut stays broken while the user still gets a
  real choice, and the full ranked list stays yours. In an attended run,
  present the three dealt structures as full cards of equal salience, the
  lead carrying kicker THE ROLL, with steer and re-roll, and let the user
  lock one in; the world is already settled, so this choice is composition.
  Visualize every dealt card: with image generation available and a
  comp-led default (.phoenix-ui/config.json buildPath; the page toggle
  handles the exception), declare a comp per card and generate after
  serving, lead first; otherwise author each card's wireframe field (see
  serve-question --schema) and the page draws the schematic. Carry the
  recorded default in the payload as buildPath with toggle: true. Locking a card
  approves its comp: a surface round that put three visualized structures on
  the table replaces the three-option comp round in visualize.md. Re-roll
  yourself only when every dealt structure fails audience identification or
  product clarity on named factual grounds.
  The assignment exists to refuse the model's ranking rut, never to outrank
  the user or the brief. Never expose assignment metadata in user-facing labels.
CHALLENGERS:
  1. A revisable sequence workshop, ordered contributions and an explicit preview build a shared result without drag-only controls.
     SOURCE ID: phoenix-experience-coauthored-sequence
     CREATIVE SPARK: Grow the shared result through understandable revisions: inspect the order, move a contribution through buttons or keys, and preview the consequence before explaining why the sequence works.
     SYSTEM GRAMMAR:
       - Palette/material: Use a quiet neutral field and warm blue active-item accent; label ownership and order readably.
       - Type/composition: Give contributions clear titles and sequence numbers; distinguish editable items from current preview.
       - Topology/navigation: Place editable order beside its result; keep the selected item and revision history discoverable.
       - Controls/state: Provide move-up, move-down, remove, and supported undo; expose conflicts rather than silently overwriting edits.
       - Responsive/motion: Stack editor and preview on mobile; retain focus after a move and make reorder motion optional.
     WEB LEVERAGE: Use ordered lists, named move controls, accessible position announcements, and conflict feedback for actual shared updates.
     MEDIA: text-only candidate; no local image supplied
  2. A reversible exploration branch, a visible path connects optional detail to the choice that opened it and preserves context on return.
     SOURCE ID: phoenix-experience-branch-return
     CREATIVE SPARK: Make a detour feel safe through a visible return: visitors can open an optional explanation, understand where they are, and return to the same choice with their place intact.
     SYSTEM GRAMMAR:
       - Palette/material: Use neutral exploration surfaces and an accessible cyan active-branch accent; label visited states.
       - Type/composition: Show each branch title and purpose; make the return label as readable as the forward choice.
       - Topology/navigation: Retain a visible path from starting choice to detail; return to the same option and preserved context.
       - Controls/state: Provide explicit back and restart; distinguish visited from completed without claiming exploration proves learning.
       - Responsive/motion: Use a single mobile path; restore return focus and provide instant transitions under reduced motion.
     WEB LEVERAGE: Use stable fragment or route states, explicit back links, accessible path navigation, and focus restoration after closing a branch.
     MEDIA: text-only candidate; no local image supplied
  3. A calm detail reveal space, optional explanations share one quiet stage while visitors choose what to inspect and when to return.
     SOURCE ID: phoenix-experience-calm-reveal
     CREATIVE SPARK: Invite deliberate inspection on a quiet stage: visitors choose a topic, inspect a bounded explanation, and return to a recognizable overview without imaginary photographs or forced animation.
     SYSTEM GRAMMAR:
       - Palette/material: Use a slate outer field and high-contrast light detail surface; one clear accent marks the selected topic.
       - Type/composition: Use short descriptive topic titles; keep explanations bounded and return actions easy to find.
       - Topology/navigation: Connect a small topic overview to one active detail region; preserve selection when visitors return.
       - Controls/state: Expose selected and closed states through text and focus; avoid hover-only reveals and automatic carousels.
       - Responsive/motion: Stack mobile overview and detail; use still changes by default and make optional transitions removable.
     WEB LEVERAGE: Use labeled disclosures, a stable detail region, visible focus, and semantic text that works without images or motion.
     MEDIA: text-only candidate; no local image supplied
  4. A light-touch practice ritual, short optional stages give a listening or language exercise a calm beginning, pause, and finish.
     SOURCE ID: phoenix-experience-light-ritual
     CREATIVE SPARK: Give brief practice a considered rhythm without taking control away: participants know what each stage asks, can pause at any point, and reach an honest finite ending.
     SYSTEM GRAMMAR:
       - Palette/material: Use warm neutral surfaces and subdued teal accents; maintain high-contrast instructions and playback state.
       - Type/composition: Use one short instruction per stage; give pause, resume, and finish consistently readable prominence.
       - Topology/navigation: Keep finite named stages with visible position and a direct path to stop or leave.
       - Controls/state: Let users control playback and pace; request permission for real microphones and do not promise therapeutic effects.
       - Responsive/motion: Keep mobile controls usable; respect reduced motion and never make animation or sound mandatory.
     WEB LEVERAGE: Use explicit media controls only with supplied assets, visible stage labels, actual recording permissions, and reduced-motion preferences.
     MEDIA: text-only candidate; no local image supplied
  5. A shared workshop choice grid, equivalent alternatives and explicit personal selection states ground collective discussion in actual choices.
     SOURCE ID: phoenix-experience-choice-grid
     CREATIVE SPARK: Make group activity legible without pretending agreement: alternatives receive equal space, each participant identifies their own choice, and shared results appear only when real data exists.
     SYSTEM GRAMMAR:
       - Palette/material: Use a light neutral board and accessible plum selection; distinguish group totals through labeled text.
       - Type/composition: Give alternatives equal title and description roles; separate personal choices from actual aggregate counts.
       - Topology/navigation: Arrange options by shared criteria; keep the discussion prompt and submission state visible nearby.
       - Controls/state: Label selected, submitted, unavailable, and pending states; never invent participant totals or consensus.
       - Responsive/motion: Stack options in the same mobile order; retain selection and remove celebratory motion on request.
     WEB LEVERAGE: Use grouped selection inputs, explicit submission feedback, and labeled totals only when backed by actual shared-session data.
     MEDIA: text-only candidate; no local image supplied
  6. A visible-rules learning exercise, a compact play field keeps the current task, legal actions, and actual outcome understandable at every step.
     SOURCE ID: phoenix-experience-visible-rules
     CREATIVE SPARK: Let play be expressive and understandable together: learners see what can be done now, receive a specific explanation of the result, and retry without hidden rules or reward theatrics.
     SYSTEM GRAMMAR:
       - Palette/material: Use a light field and two accessible task/result accents; express correctness through readable text.
       - Type/composition: Give the challenge a strong heading; keep short rules and specific feedback close to the action.
       - Topology/navigation: Keep task, legal actions, and recent outcome in one bounded field with a clear restart path.
       - Controls/state: Show valid, invalid, incomplete, and completed states honestly; permit rule inspection before answering.
       - Responsive/motion: Use one mobile column; provide keyboard input and a still alternative to any optional result animation.
     WEB LEVERAGE: Use semantic forms, accessible validation, keyboard-operable actions, and a result region announced only when it changes.
     MEDIA: text-only candidate; no local image supplied
A challenger wins only when its fused result beats the grounded list on
  audience identification and product clarity. It may change task topology or
  interaction, but never the committed visual identity.
Compare supplied local images only when they exist. A text-only candidate has no visual reference; do not invent a board or contact a remote image service.
PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md constrain every surface candidate's identity
vocabulary; they do not cancel task-level composition. The seed never
authorizes a new palette, type system, material world, or unfamiliar control
behavior.
The CREATIVE SPARK is a complete visual system, not a theme or decorative
reference. Translate every supplied system rule into the product: palette and
material, type and composition, topology, controls and states, and adaptation.
Keep the source's visible character, scale, rhythm, and interaction instead of
reducing vivid grammar to generic nouns. Keep a literal carrier only when it
becomes functional.
Ambitious motion, spatial media, or interaction is welcome when it strengthens
the product without weakening semantics, performance, or fallback behavior.
MODE RULES (experience, from <REPO>/tests/fixtures/mode-rules-skill/reference/mode-persuade.md). They govern this surface's directions and every comp you write or judge for it, the decision comps included; where shared guidance conflicts, these win.
DIRECTIONS
- PERSUADE DIRECTION RULE ONE.
- PERSUADE DIRECTION RULE TWO.
COMPS
- PERSUADE COMP RULE.
A user- or brief-pinned decision beats the roll, always.
